claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex
expected_eligibility.reason: Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To assess your eligibility, I need to know about the children you're claiming for. Let me ask:

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Specifically:
- Are they **under 16 years old**?
- Are they **16 to 19 years old**?
- Are they **20 years old or over**?

Please let me know the age(s) of the child/children, and if you have multiple children, please tell me about each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're asking about **Alex, who is 8 years old** and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, let me continue with the next part of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in any paid work?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I expect the answer is that he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's just at primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's exactly what I expected. Alex is at primary school and not in any paid work, so he meets this requirement.

Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, is he not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

These are benefits claimed directly by the child themselves. For an 8-year-old, the answer would typically be no - he wouldn't be receiving these - but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He's just 8, so nothing like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits, so he meets this requirement too.

Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, he wouldn't be in an apprenticeship at all. But I need to confirm: Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 and in primary school. No apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Absolutely, that makes sense! Alex is clearly not in an apprenticeship at all.

Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. There are several possible paths that can qualify you. Let me ask:

**Where do you normally live?**

- Do you **normally live in the UK**?
- Or do you have a specific immigration status like:
  - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
  - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (if so, we may need to explore what your situation is)?
  - Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

For most people, the answer is simply that they normally live in the UK. Is that your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Leeds.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You normally live in the UK in Leeds, so you meet the residency requirement.

Let me continue to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

"Responsible" means one of the following:
- You **live with the child** (which you've already told me - Alex lives with you at home)
- OR you're **contributing to their upkeep** (paying for their food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)
- OR you're **paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Since you've already mentioned Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet this requirement. Can you confirm that you live with Alex and are responsible for his care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me at home and I look after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You live with Alex and look after him, so you're clearly responsible for him.

Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question: **Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim Child Benefit for him?**

For example:
- Is his other parent claiming for him?
- Is another family member or guardian claiming for him?
- Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him - just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Where does Alex live?**

- Is he living with you at home normally?
- Or is he in hospital at the moment?
- Or is he in a care facility?
- Or is he in a fostering arrangement?

Based on what you've told me so far, I expect Alex is living with you at home normally, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in the hospital for a while now - he's been there for about 3 or 4 months.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. So Alex has been in hospital for about 3 or 4 months. Let me get the next set of rules to check the specific duration requirements for children in hospital.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, I have the rules. So Alex has been in hospital for 3-4 months, which is within the 12-week cumulative limit.

I need to ask a few clarifying questions about his hospital stay:

**1. Has this been one continuous stay in hospital for 3-4 months?** Or has he had multiple stays (times where he left hospital and came back)?

**2. If there have been multiple stays:** How long was the gap between each stay? Was it more or less than 28 days?

The reason I'm asking is there's a special rule: if Alex leaves hospital and returns within 28 days, the time counts towards the total. But if he's been away for 28 days or more before returning, the counter resets.

For now, can you clarify whether this has been one continuous 3-4 month stay?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been one continuous stay - he's been there the whole time, about 15 weeks now actually.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for about 15 weeks now.

This is important: the rules say that Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks while a child is in hospital. Since Alex has now been in hospital for 15 weeks (which exceeds the 12-week limit), I need to check if you're regularly spending money on him to support him.

Let me ask: **Are you regularly spending money on Alex's upkeep while he's in hospital?**

For example:
- Do you buy him clothes, toiletries, or other personal items?
- Do you contribute towards his pocket money or spending money?
- Do you pay for anything else to support him (like entertainment, gifts, etc.)?

If you're regularly spending enough money on him that equals or exceeds the current Child Benefit rate, you may still be eligible even though he's exceeded the 12-week limit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been able to afford to spend money on things for him while he's been in there. It's been really difficult financially.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand, that must be a difficult situation. Let me navigate through the assessment with this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on what you've told me - that you haven't been able to afford to spend money on things for Alex while he's been in hospital - you don't meet the exception to the 12-week rule.

Let me confirm the outcome with you:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you of this outcome. Based on the assessment, **you are currently ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Alex has been in hospital continuously for about 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit for Child Benefit while a child is in hospital. The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 12 weeks in hospital, but after that point, you would need to be regularly spending money on Alex's upkeep (at least the equivalent of the current Child Benefit rate) to remain eligible.

Since you've indicated you haven't been able to afford to spend money on him during his hospital stay, you don't qualify for the exception to the 12-week rule.

**Important guidance:**

- However, if your circumstances change and you do start regularly spending money on Alex (for example, if financial circumstances improve), you may become eligible again.
- If Alex leaves hospital and you take him home again, you would regain eligibility for Child Benefit from that point onwards.
- There may be other support available to you - I'd recommend contacting **HMRC directly** on **0300 200 3100** to discuss your situation and ask about any exceptions or alternative support.
- You could also look into other benefits you might be entitled to, such as help with childcare costs or other family support.

I understand this is difficult news, particularly during a challenging time with Alex in hospital. Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So basically because he's been in hospital for more than 12 weeks and I'm not spending money on him regularly, I don't qualify right now. But if things change - like if he comes home or if I'm able to start buying things for him - then I might be eligible again?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, exactly! You've understood it correctly.

**Your situation:**
- Right now, you're ineligible because Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks (15 weeks) and you're not regularly spending money on him.

**But eligibility could change if:**

1. **Alex leaves the hospital and comes home to live with you again** - If he's discharged and returns home, you would regain eligibility for Child Benefit from that point onwards. The 12-week clock would essentially "reset" once he's out of hospital.

2. **Your financial circumstances improve and you're able to spend money on him regularly** - If you start regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital (buying him clothes, toiletries, pocket money, gifts, etc.) at a level that equals or exceeds the current Child Benefit rate, you could become eligible again even while he's still in hospital.

3. **If he has another hospital stay in the future** - The 12-week limit applies to each hospital stay. If he's discharged and stays out for 28 days or more before going back to hospital, it would be treated as a new stay with a fresh 12-week allowance.

**What you should do:**

- **Contact HMRC on 0300 200 3100** to report any changes in Alex's circumstances (when he leaves hospital, or if you start spending money on him).
- Keep them informed of his status so your claim can be updated when things change.
- In the meantime, ask about other financial support you might be eligible for to help during this difficult time.

I hope Alex makes a good recovery and is able to come home soon. Is there anything else I can help you with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's really helpful - thank you for explaining it all so clearly. I'll contact HMRC if anything changes with Alex's situation. I appreciate your help.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help explain the situation clearly. You've been very straightforward with all the information, which made the assessment straightforward.

**To summarize your eligibility outcome:**

Let me formally record this assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Your assessment has been recorded.

**Key contacts if you need further support:**

- **HMRC Child Benefit:** 0300 200 3100
- **Gov.uk Child Benefit information:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

**Remember to get in touch with HMRC when:**
- Alex is discharged from hospital
- Your financial circumstances change
- You need to discuss any other support available to you

I hope Alex recovers well and that your situation improves. Take care, and don't hesitate to reach out if you have any other questions!

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and meets the basic eligibility criteria as a qualifying child (under 16, not working full-time, not receiving benefits in his own right, not in a disqualifying apprenticeship). The claimant also meets residency requirements (living in the UK in Leeds), is responsible for Alex (he lives with them at home), and there are no other claimants. However, Alex has been in hospital continuously for approximately 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit for Child Benefit eligibility during hospital stays. The exception to this 12-week rule would apply if the claimant was regularly spending money on Alex's upkeep while in hospital, but the claimant has indicated they have not been able to afford to do so. Therefore, Alex is currently ineligible for Child Benefit under the hospital duration rules.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex due to the child exceeding the 12-week hospital stay limit without regular financial support being provided. While all other eligibility criteria are met, the extended hospital stay (15 weeks) combined with no regular spending on the child's upkeep triggers the ineligibility rule. The claimant should contact HMRC if Alex is discharged from hospital or if their financial circumstances change to allow them to support Alex during his stay."
